title: Zarokh, the Temporal Boss Guide: Trial Access, Honour and Time Mechanics
summary: Complete Trial of the Sekhemas floor 4 boss guide covering Barya entry, Honour management, the Clock hourglass phase, Relic priority, and the time-stop phase.
description: Learn how to reach and beat Zarokh in the Trial of the Sekhemas with floor-by-floor access, Honour tips, Relic priorities and phase strategy.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team

sections.title: What You Need to Know Before Attempting Zarokh
sections.callout: The boss itself is manageable. Reaching the boss is the real challenge.
calloutDetail: Zarokh sits at the end of a four-floor trial with an Honour system that can end your run before you ever see the boss.
Preparation for the trial floors matters more than raw DPS for the boss fight itself.
Zarokh triggers a Clock phase: 6 hourglasses spawn around the arena and must be collected within one rotation.
Since 0.3.0, missing an hourglass no longer instantly fails the Trial—it deals Honour damage and triggers a slowed sub-phase instead.

answers.label: Access
answers.text: You need a Barya to enter. The trial has four floors with escalating difficulty and Honour loss on hits taken.

answers.label: Honour
answers.text: Honour is your trial HP. Losing all Honour ends the run. Prioritise Honour resistance and avoidance over damage.

answers.label: The boss
answers.text: Zarokh has a time-stop phase where you must keep moving. Do not stand still during the temporal field.

sections.title: Trial Access: Floors, Barya and Honour

facts.label: Entry item
facts.note: Barya drops from endgame maps. You need one per attempt.

facts.label: Structure
facts.note: Each floor has rooms with enemies, traps and choices. Floor 4 ends at Zarokh.

facts.label: Honour system
facts.note: Taking hits loses Honour. Zero Honour ends the run immediately. Honour does not regenerate between floors.

facts.label: On failure
facts.value: Lose the Barya and all trial progress
facts.note: You must start from floor 1 with a new Barya. No checkpoints within a run.

steps.label: Obtain a Barya
body: Barya items drop from endgame maps. You need at least one to enter the Trial of the Sekhemas.

steps.label: Clear floors 1–3
body: Each floor has rooms with combat encounters, traps and reward choices. Prioritise Honour preservation over greed. Avoid unnecessary fights when possible.

steps.label: Reach floor 4 and enter the boss room
body: Floor 4 leads directly to Zarokh. Enter with as much Honour as possible. There is no recovery between floor 4 rooms and the boss.

sections.title: Preparation: Relics, Honour Resistance and Build Checks

items.label: Honour resistance Relics
checks: Reduce Honour loss per hit taken during the trial floors.
items.why: Honour loss accumulates across four floors. Even small reductions compound significantly over a full run.
items.fix: Prioritise Relics with Honour resistance for your first attempts. Damage Relics become relevant once you can consistently reach the boss.

items.label: Movement and avoidance
checks: The trial floors have traps and ambushes that cost Honour.
items.why: Most Honour loss happens on the floors, not the boss. Avoidance is more valuable than tanking.
items.fix: Use a movement skill to reposition quickly. Do not face-tank trap rooms.

items.label: Single-target damage for the boss
checks: Zarokh has a substantial HP pool. Longer fights mean more time-stop phases.
items.why: Each time-stop phase is a survival check. Shorter fights mean fewer checks.
items.fix: Bring a dedicated single-target setup. Verify support gem compatibility.

items.label: Lightning and physical defence
checks: Zarokh deals both physical and lightning damage.
items.why: The time-stop phase has lightning attacks that are hard to avoid while repositioning.
items.fix: Cap lightning resistance if possible. Bring a physical damage reduction option.

phases.label: Phase 1: Standard Combat
objectives: Learn the melee combo and ranged projectile patterns.
Stay mobile — do not commit to long attack animations.
Save defensive cooldowns for the time-stop phase.
notes: Phase one is a standard boss fight with physical melee combos and occasional ranged projectiles.
The key is resource conservation. Do not use all your defensive tools here — you will need them in phase two.

phases.label: Phase 2: Clock phase (collect hourglasses)
phases.trigger: Mid-fight Zarokh stops time and spawns 6 hourglasses (hourglass) around the arena.
objectives: Collect all 6 hourglasses within one rotation (one full spin).
If you miss one, keep moving to grab the rest—don't stand still.
Once collected, time resumes and the standard fight continues.
notes: The 6 hourglasses sit around the arena edge and must be picked up before Zarokh completes one rotation.
0.3.0 change: missing an hourglass no longer instantly fails the Trial. Instead it deals Honour damage and triggers a slowed sub-phase; you can keep fighting.
A single miss is survivable, but repeated misses stack Honour pressure and can still end the attempt.

phases.label: Phase 2: Temporal Field (Time Stop)
phases.trigger: HP drops below approximately 50%. Zarokh creates a temporal field.
objectives: Keep moving during the time-stop field — standing still is lethal.
Identify the safe movement paths between temporal zones.
Use short attacks between movement cycles.
notes: The time-stop phase slows or freezes parts of the arena. You must keep moving through safe corridors.
Lightning attacks continue during the time-stop. They are harder to see because the visual field changes.
This phase repeats if you do not kill Zarokh quickly enough. Each repetition increases pressure.

attacks.name: Temporal Slash
telegraph: Weapon glows and a short wind-up precedes a wide arc.
responses: Step back or dodge through the arc. The recovery is short.
commonMistakes: Standing in melee range without watching the wind-up.

attacks.name: Temporal Projectile
telegraph: Zarokh raises his staff and a glowing orb forms.
responses: Move laterally. The projectile tracks briefly but can be outrun.
commonMistakes: Running straight away — the tracking catches you. Go sideways.
notes: Also used during the time-stop phase, making it harder to see.

attacks.name: Temporal Field (Time Stop)
telegraph: The arena shifts colour and parts of the ground freeze.
responses: Keep moving through unfrozen corridors. Do not stand still.
commonMistakes: Panicking and running into a frozen zone, which roots you.
notes: The frozen zones deal damage and root you. Only the moving corridors are safe.

attacks.name: Temporal Lightning Strike
telegraph: Brief ground marker appears during the time-stop field.
responses: Keep moving — do not stop to dodge. The corridor movement avoids most strikes.
commonMistakes: Stopping to dodge-roll, which puts you in a frozen zone.
notes: These strikes are secondary threats during the time-stop. Movement is the primary survival tool.

attacks.name: Clock Hourglasses
telegraph: Arena shifts color; 6 hourglasses appear around the edges.
responses: Pick them up one by one within the rotation; if you miss one, keep moving for the rest—don't freeze in place.
notes: Since 0.3.0 a missed hourglass deals Honour damage and triggers a slowed sub-phase rather than an instant fail.
commonMistakes: Chasing one hourglass into the time-stop zone.

sections.title: Build Considerations
paragraphs: The trial floors are the real DPS check, not the boss. Bring enough clear speed to handle floor enemies quickly without taking unnecessary Honour damage.
For the boss itself, single-target damage reduces the number of time-stop phases you must survive. Every additional phase is another survival check.
Movement speed and movement skills are doubly valuable: they help on the trial floors (avoiding traps) and during the time-stop phase (navigating corridors).
Minion builds should ensure minions can follow through the time-stop corridors. Some minion AI may path poorly through frozen zones.
bullets: First attempts should prioritise Honour preservation Relics over damage Relics.
Once you can consistently reach the boss, swap to damage-focused Relics to shorten the fight.

entries.question: Why is the trial harder than the actual boss?
summary: Players frequently report dying on the floors before reaching Zarokh. The Honour system makes the approach more punishing than the fight itself.
editorialAnalysis: This is by design — the trial is meant to test consistency, not just boss knowledge. The guide should validate this frustration while providing concrete Honour-preservation strategies.
officialAnswer: The floors are the primary challenge. Prioritise Honour resistance Relics, avoid unnecessary fights, and learn trap patterns. The boss becomes manageable once you arrive with high Honour.

entries.question: What do I actually do during the time-stop phase?
summary: Players describe confusion about where to move during the temporal field. The visual change makes it hard to identify safe corridors.
editorialAnalysis: The time-stop phase needs a clear movement instruction rather than vague advice. Players need to know: keep moving, follow unfrozen ground, do not stop to dodge.
officialAnswer: Keep moving through unfrozen corridors. Do not stop to dodge-roll — continuous movement through safe ground is the survival mechanic. Lightning strikes are secondary; the frozen zones are the primary threat.

problems.symptom: I keep losing all Honour before reaching the boss.
directAnswer: Most Honour loss comes from unnecessary fights and trap rooms on floors 1–3. You do not need to clear every room.
checks: Skip optional combat rooms when possible.
Use movement skills to traverse trap rooms without taking hits.
Equip Honour resistance Relics for your first several attempts.

problems.symptom: The time-stop phase kills me every time.
directAnswer: You are likely stopping to dodge or running into frozen zones. The correct response is continuous movement through unfrozen corridors.
checks: Do not dodge-roll during the time-stop — keep walking/running.
Accept that you will take some lightning hits — movement avoids the lethal frozen zones.

directAnswer: For first attempts: Honour resistance. Once you consistently reach the boss: damage. The trial is designed so that survival Relics enable reaching the boss, and damage Relics shorten the fight.
checks: Start with Honour resistance Relics until you can reach floor 4 consistently.
Swap to damage Relics once the floors are manageable.
Do not mix both unless you have a large Relic inventory.

rewards.label: Ascendancy Point
notes: Completing the Trial of the Sekhemas grants an ascendancy point. This is one of the primary sources of ascendancy points in the game.

rewards.label: Trial Reward Room
notes: The reward room after Zarokh contains equipment and currency. Quality depends on floor choices made during the run.
